eagle_wings.title: Clayface
eagle_wings.description: Rising Hollywood star Matt Hagen descends into a horrifying revenge-filled monster when scientific ambition strips him of his identity and humanity

eagle_wings.title: Wildwood
eagle_wings.description: The adventures of Prue McKeel as she sets off to the forests outside Portland to find her kidnapped brother

eagle_wings.title: Street Fighter
eagle_wings.description: Street Fighters Ryu and Ken reunite when Chun-Li recruits them for the World Warrior Tournament. As they face a hidden conspiracy, they must confront each other and their past-or face destruction

eagle_wings.title: Whalefall
eagle_wings.description: Follows a scuba diver who, while looking for his father's remains, is swallowed by an 80-foot, 60-ton sperm whale and has just one hour to get out before his oxygen runs out

eagle_wings.title: Pace
eagle_wings.description: Fresh out of rehab, Malcolm, a 40-year old former addict, looks for purpose in his late brother’s passion for running. But confronted with unresolved family expectations, a judgmental society, and destructive self-loathing, can Malcolm keep pace, or will he succumb to the unrelen...

filmhouse.title: The Invite
filmhouse.description: You’re cordially invited to the most chaotic dinner of the year. Fresh from its buzz heavy Sundance debut, Olivia Wilde’s razor sharp relationship comedy hits right where it hurts. Joe (Seth Rogen) and Angela (Wilde) are stuck in a domestic rut, made worse by the aggressively loud, boundary pushing love life of their upstairs neighbors, Hawk (Edward Norton) and Pina (Penélope Cruz). Hoping to smooth things over, Angela invites them down for a casual dinner party. But as the wine flows, polite small talk is instantly traded for a chaotic, hilariously uncomfortable truth game where social etiquette completely crumbles. In English Rated M18 for Mature Content and Coarse Language.

filmhouse.title: A Poet
filmhouse.description: Oscar is an aging, rueful poet whose artistic ambitions have long faded into obscurity and heavy drinking. When Oscar takes up teaching to meet ends meet, he encounters Yurlady, a working-class girl with an extraordinary gift for poetry, he becomes consumed with launching her talent into the local literary scene. Driven by a desperate longing for career redemption and a second chance at fatherhood, Oscar inadvertently pushes her into an ambitious world she never asked to join. Directed by Simón Mesa Soto, this tragicomedy earned the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at the Cannes Film Festival and represented Colombia as its official submission for Best International Feature Film. Anchored by a brilliant, cringe-inducing performance from Ubeimar Rios, the film offers a darkly funny and deeply humane satire on artist egos and the messy search for purpose. A Poet, A Creative, A Panel Join us for a post-show fireside chat on Tue 6 Oct, 7.30pm ! Do you dream of writing your story one day? Of writing novels, poetry, or making films? Do you want to support those dreamers around us to do so? It isn’t easy being an artist anywhere, especially not outside major commercial systems like America, the UK, and Hollywood. And though A POET comes from halfway across the world, our creative industries are really not so different. So why make the admirably Herculean task of creating any harder by keeping career wisdom behind closed doors (or gates), or by having to struggle alone? And if you care about local voices, then how can we best support our artists? Join us for a fireside chat with a local poet, Theophilus Kwek , and filmmaker, Pek Jia Hao , as they share with us their uncensored stories, tips and tricks, and dreams for the creative life in Singapore. In Spanish with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Nudity.

filmhouse.title: Fjord
filmhouse.description: The Gheorghius, a devout Romanian Norwegian couple, resettle in a village set in a distant fjord where they become close to their neighbours, the Halbergs. Their children bond despite their different education. When adolescent Elia Gheorghiu shows up at school with some bruises on her body, the community asks itself if the traditional education that the Gheorghiu children get from their parents might have anything to do with it. Winner of the Palme d’Or at the Cannes Film Festival, Fjord marks another masterclass in moral ambiguity from director Cristian Mungiu (4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, R.M.N.). Anchored by magnetic, career-defining performances from Stan and Reinsve, the film dissects the terrifying machinery of state intervention with surgical narrative precision. Framed in stark long-take cinematography that captures the icy, claustrophobic grandeur of its Scandinavian setting, Fjord is an explosive, thought-provoking drama bound to spark debate. In Romanian and Norwegian with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Some Nudity. TW: Contains depictions of self-harm.

filmhouse.title: Kokuho
filmhouse.description: Following its phenomenal success in Japan, critically acclaimed film Kokuho is enjoying a re-release in Singapore with limited screenings! Directed by acclaimed filmmaker Lee Sang-il and adapted from Shuichi Yoshida's bestselling novel of the same name, Kokuho stars Ryo Yoshizawa and Ryusei Yokohama alongside an impressive ensemble cast including Ken Watanabe. Set in the fascinating world of Kabuki, Japan's centuries-old traditional performing art, Kokuho tells the story of two young men from very different backgrounds whose lives become intertwined through their pursuit perfecting their craft. More than just a story about performance, Kokuho is a powerful portrait of ambition, identity and the price of dedicating one's life to art. Recognised by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, Kabuki is celebrated for its rich traditions, elaborate costumes and stylised performances. One of its most iconic features is “onnagata”, the art of male actors portraying female roles with extraordinary precision, grace and emotional depth. Since its release, Kokuho has become the highest-grossing live-action Japanese film in history. Domestic and global popularity of the film has also rekindled public interest in kabuki. The film dominated the 49th Japan Academy Film Prize, taking home ten awards, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor. Its exceptional Kabuki-inspired hair and makeup artistry also earned a nomination for Best Makeup and Hairstyling at the 98th Academy Awards, bringing the beauty of Japanese traditional culture to the global stage. In Japanese with English and Mandarin dual subtitles. Rated M18 for Sexual Scenes.

filmhouse.title: The Violinist
filmhouse.description: Set across the shifting landscape of colonial Singapore and wartime Malaya, two musically gifted childhood friends—Fei and Kai—are bound together by their shared devotion to the violin. When the brutal onset of World War II and the Japanese Occupation tears them apart, Fei embarks on a decades-long journey across a changing Southeast Asia, holding onto memory, resilience, and the power of music as she searches for her lost friend. A landmark achievement for local cinema, co-directors Ervin Han and Raúl García’s hand-drawn feature made history by winning the prestigious Cristal Award for Best Feature at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival, alongside the SACEM Award for Best Original Soundtrack. Blending meticulous traditional craft with an evocative score by Ricky Ho, the film transforms regional history into a deeply human, universally resonant story that demands to be experienced on the big screen Director Q&A, Sunday 4 Oct Join us for an in-person Q&A with Co-Director Ervin Han , alongside Art Director and Storyboard Artist Ong Ruwei , Character Designer Sakura Wong and Animation Supervisor Wendy Li . In English with English and Mandarin subtitles. Rated PG for Some Violence

filmhouse.title: Fjord
filmhouse.description: The Gheorghius, a devout Romanian Norwegian couple, resettle in a village set in a distant fjord where they become close to their neighbours, the Halbergs. Their children bond despite their different education. When adolescent Elia Gheorghiu shows up at school with some bruises on her body, the community asks itself if the traditional education that the Gheorghiu children get from their parents might have anything to do with it. Winner of the Palme d’Or at the Cannes Film Festival, Fjord marks another masterclass in moral ambiguity from director Cristian Mungiu (4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, R.M.N.). Anchored by magnetic, career-defining performances from Stan and Reinsve, the film dissects the terrifying machinery of state intervention with surgical narrative precision. Framed in stark long-take cinematography that captures the icy, claustrophobic grandeur of its Scandinavian setting, Fjord is an explosive, thought-provoking drama bound to spark debate. In Romanian and Norwegian with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Some Nudity. TW: Contains depictions of self-harm.

filmhouse.title: Hereditary
filmhouse.description: Following the death of her secretive mother, miniature artist Annie Graham attempts to navigate her family's complex grief while maintaining a semblance of order in her secluded home. As disturbing, unexplainable events begin to target her children, the family plunges into a nightmare of escalating trauma, revealing sinister secrets about their ancestry. Directed by Ari Aster in his astonishing feature debut, this modern horror masterpiece captivated audiences and critics alike, earning Toni Collette widespread acclaim for her staggering central performance. Blending agonizing familial drama with relentless, visceral dread, the film crafts a haunting exploration of inherited trauma and inescapable fate. In English with Mandarin subtitles. Rated M18 for Some Nudity. TW: Contains depictions of self harm, animal cruelty and graphic scenes.

filmhouse.title: What We Do in the Shadows
filmhouse.description: In modern-day Wellington, New Zealand, a group of centuries-old vampires share a suburban flat and struggle with the mundane realities of modren domestic life. When a camera crew documents their daily routines, the arrival of a newly turned vampire and his human software-engineer friend introduces the ancient flatmates to contemporary culture, forcing them to adapt to the 21st century. Driven by razor-sharp improvisation, deadpan comedy, and inventive visual gags, this Taika Waititi classic offers a brilliant, endearing subversion of classic creature-feature tropes, earning its status as a cult classic. In English. Rated NC16 for Some Violence and Nudity.

filmhouse.title: Love Letter (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: Still grieving the tragic loss of her fiancé Itsuki Fujii in a mountain climbing accident, Hiroko Watanabe sends a letter to his old childhood address in snow-covered Otaru, a home she believes no longer exists, hoping to send a message into the ether. To her shock, she receives a reply signed by "Itsuki Fujii." The respondent is not her late lover's ghost, but a female former classmate who shared his exact name. As the two women begin exchanging letters across the snowbound landscape, a tender, long buried portrait of forgotten youth, unrequited first love, and shared memory slowly unfurls. A foundational landmark of 1990s Asian cinema, Shunji Iwai’s feature debut became a massive cultural phenomenon across East and Southeast Asia, immortalized by Miho Nakayama’s double performance. Shot with a dreamlike, soft focus palette by the late cinematographer Noboru Shinoda, this new 4K digital restoration preserves every delicate detail. 4K remastering under the supervision of Fuji Television Network, Inc., with all analog and digital processes by Imagica Entertainment Media Services, Inc. Image digitization through high-resolution 4K scanning from the original 35mm camera negative. Restoration, color correction, and final sound finishing supervised by director Shunji Iwai. In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated PG Presented at Filmhouse as part of Japanese Film Festival, in partnership with the Singapore Film Society, Japan Creative Center and Japan Foundation

filmhouse.title: Monster House
filmhouse.description: On the eve of Halloween, three young friends discover that the eerie, dilapidated home across the street owned by an old recluse is actually a living, breathing entity with a lethal appetite for anyone who steps onto its lawn. When the adults dismiss their frantic warnings, the trio must band together to infiltrate and destroy the living house before trick-or-treaters flood the neighborhood. Directed by Gil Kenan, this Academy Award-nominated animated feature combines innovative performance-capture technology with genuine scares and emotional depth, capturing the nostalgic thrill of childhood fears mixed with unexpected empathy. In English. Rated PG.

filmhouse.title: OSFF 2026 Focus | Image & Memory: Early Works of Hirokazu Kore-eda
filmhouse.description: Objectifs Short Film Festival presents: Focus | Image & Memory: Early Works of Hirokazu Kore-eda Focus presents the early short films of a key international filmmaker. The showcase will consist of rarely seen short films, with a post-screening Q&A with the filmmaker. Objectifs is proud to be able to feature two of film auteur Hirokazu Kore-eda 's earlier documentaries, Lessons from a Calf and Where Has All The Pollution Gone? for the inaugural edition of the Objectifs Short Film Festival. Known for his seminal works like Maborosi, Nobody Knows and Shoplifters , Kore-eda’s inception as a director came about through television documentaries that he directed and conceptualised in 1987 for NONFIX, a late-night documentary series that was broadcasted on Fuji Television. The opportunity and experimentation afforded through work for NONFIX, which included Lessons from a Calf and Where Has All The Pollution Gone? led to Kore-eda’s perennial fascination with an image’s potential to communicate intention, as well as elicit emotion. As observed through his later fictional films, Kore-eda’s hallmark ability to harness an ironically steely eye in order to garner empathy for issues pertaining to social realism has evident roots in his earlier television work. Witness the beginnings of Hirokazu Kore-eda's journey as a filmmaker in this rare chance to watch his early films, as well as trace his directing methodology from the initial craft of documentary, all with the filmmaker himself in attendance. Lessons From A Calf / 47 min / Japan / 1991 In 1988, Ina Elementary School adopted a cow named Laura from a ranch as a part of the school’s integrated learning program. Students learn from building the cow’s barn, calculating the feed cost and debating in class for making decisions. Capturing the kids’ lively expressions, the documentary witnesses their growth through the care of Laura. Kore-eda’s first project, mostly rolling a video camera by himself. Where Has All The Pollution Gone? / 47 min / Japan / 1992 In early 1960s Chiba, pollution from a steel factory left locals with asthma. Ministry of Environment bureaucrat Hashimoto Michio became a hero after drafting Japan's first pollution control law in 1967. But as certified patients multiplied and compensation costs strained the economy, the government deregulated the law, declaring the pollution resolved. Because of this, Hashimoto was recast as a traitor by victims who knew otherwise. Supported by Filmhouse Ticket price: $25 Buy Tickets: https://osff-25oct.peatix.com/

filmhouse.title: Moonlight (10th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: Framed across three pivotal eras of his life, Chiron navigates the harsh realities of growing up in a tough neighborhood while struggling with his identity, sexuality, and a troubled home environment. Guided by the tender mentorship of a local drug dealer and a deep, enduring connection with a childhood friend, Chiron gradually leanrs to protect himself from the world as he grows into adulthood. Directed by Barry Jenkins, this groundbreaking drama won three Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Supporting Actor for Mahershala Ali. Celebrated for James Laxton’s luminous cinematography and Nicholas Britell’s evocative score, the film stands as a transcendent, deeply lyrical portrait of intimacy, vulnerability, and self-discovery. Newly restored in 4K and with an exclusive conversation with director Barry Jenkins, featuring Oscar Nominated composer Nicholas Britell and Oscar winner Mahershala Ali, to follow the feature. In English. Rated M18 for Some Homosexual Content.

filmhouse.title: La La Land (10th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: Mia, an aspiring actress, serves lattes to movie stars in between auditions and Sebastian, a jazz musician, scrapes by playing cocktail party gigs in dingy bars, but as success mounts they are faced with decisions that begin to fray the fragile fabric of their love affair, and the dreams they worked so hard to maintain in each other threaten to rip them apart. In English with Mandarin Subtitles Rated PG13 for Some Coarse Language

filmhouse.title: Kokuho
filmhouse.description: Following its phenomenal success in Japan, critically acclaimed film Kokuho is enjoying a re-release in Singapore with limited screenings! Directed by acclaimed filmmaker Lee Sang-il and adapted from Shuichi Yoshida's bestselling novel of the same name, Kokuho stars Ryo Yoshizawa and Ryusei Yokohama alongside an impressive ensemble cast including Ken Watanabe. Set in the fascinating world of Kabuki, Japan's centuries-old traditional performing art, Kokuho tells the story of two young men from very different backgrounds whose lives become intertwined through their pursuit perfecting their craft. More than just a story about performance, Kokuho is a powerful portrait of ambition, identity and the price of dedicating one's life to art. Recognised by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, Kabuki is celebrated for its rich traditions, elaborate costumes and stylised performances. One of its most iconic features is “onnagata”, the art of male actors portraying female roles with extraordinary precision, grace and emotional depth. Since its release, Kokuho has become the highest-grossing live-action Japanese film in history. Domestic and global popularity of the film has also rekindled public interest in kabuki. The film dominated the 49th Japan Academy Film Prize, taking home ten awards, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor. Its exceptional Kabuki-inspired hair and makeup artistry also earned a nomination for Best Makeup and Hairstyling at the 98th Academy Awards, bringing the beauty of Japanese traditional culture to the global stage. In Japanese with English and Mandarin dual subtitles. Rated M18 for Sexual Scenes.

filmhouse.title: Fjord
filmhouse.description: The Gheorghius, a devout Romanian Norwegian couple, resettle in a village set in a distant fjord where they become close to their neighbours, the Halbergs. Their children bond despite their different education. When adolescent Elia Gheorghiu shows up at school with some bruises on her body, the community asks itself if the traditional education that the Gheorghiu children get from their parents might have anything to do with it. Winner of the Palme d’Or at the Cannes Film Festival, Fjord marks another masterclass in moral ambiguity from director Cristian Mungiu (4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, R.M.N.). Anchored by magnetic, career-defining performances from Stan and Reinsve, the film dissects the terrifying machinery of state intervention with surgical narrative precision. Framed in stark long-take cinematography that captures the icy, claustrophobic grandeur of its Scandinavian setting, Fjord is an explosive, thought-provoking drama bound to spark debate. In Romanian and Norwegian with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Some Nudity. TW: Contains depictions of self-harm.

filmhouse.title: The Violinist
filmhouse.description: Set across the shifting landscape of colonial Singapore and wartime Malaya, two musically gifted childhood friends—Fei and Kai—are bound together by their shared devotion to the violin. When the brutal onset of World War II and the Japanese Occupation tears them apart, Fei embarks on a decades-long journey across a changing Southeast Asia, holding onto memory, resilience, and the power of music as she searches for her lost friend. A landmark achievement for local cinema, co-directors Ervin Han and Raúl García’s hand-drawn feature made history by winning the prestigious Cristal Award for Best Feature at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival, alongside the SACEM Award for Best Original Soundtrack. Blending meticulous traditional craft with an evocative score by Ricky Ho, the film transforms regional history into a deeply human, universally resonant story that demands to be experienced on the big screen Director Q&A, Sunday 4 Oct Join us for an in-person Q&A with Co-Director Ervin Han , alongside Art Director and Storyboard Artist Ong Ruwei , Character Designer Sakura Wong and Animation Supervisor Wendy Li . In English with English and Mandarin subtitles. Rated PG for Some Violence

filmhouse.title: Perfect Days
filmhouse.description: Hirayama works as a cleaner of public toilets in Tokyo, leading a quiet, contentment-driven life structured around classic rock cassettes, secondhand books, and photographing the light filtering through urban trees. As small, unexpected encounters break his daily routine, quiet details of his past gradually come to light. Directed by Wim Wenders, this Oscar nominee for Best International Feature earned Kōji Yakusho the Best Actor prize at the Cannes Film Festival. Celebrating the dignity of labor and the art of mindfulness, the film offers a warm, contemplative, and visually striking observation of contemporary Tokyo. In Japanese with English subitles. Rated PG for Brief Nudity

filmhouse.title: Digger
filmhouse.description: Digger Rockwell (Tom Cruise) is a megalomaniacal oil tycoon and one of the most powerful men on the planet. When his reckless deep-sea drilling operation in Greenland triggers a catastrophic environmental disaster, Digger refuses to back down or accept blame. Instead, he launches a frantic, delusional public relations crusade to spin the catastrophe, attempting to convince an unraveling world that he is humanity’s ultimate savior before the consequences of his hubris destroy everything. Four-time Academy Award winner Alejandro González Iñárritu ( Birdman , The Revenant ) returns to English language filmmaking with a blistering, absurdist black comedy. Anchored by Cruise’s most unhinged, transformative lead performance in decades, the film features a stellar supporting ensemble including Sandra Hüller, Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, and Jesse Plemons. Shot entirely on 35mm VistaVision by master cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki, Digger pairs razor sharp political satire with sweeping visual scale, an audacious, large-format spectacle engineered specifically for the big screen experience. In English with English & Chinese subtitles Rated M18 for Coarse Language.

filmhouse.title: Tony
filmhouse.description: Discover how the iconic Anthony Bourdain came to be in Matt Johnson’s scrappy coming-of-age comedy that's equal parts sweet and sour. Long before he became the world’s favorite culinary storyteller, Anthony Bourdain was just a dishwashing kid getting baptized in the grease, sweat, and chaos of a 1970s coastal seafood shack. This electric origin story follows a young Tony (Dominic Sessa) as he gets thrown into the fire of a cutthroat kitchen brigade. Surrounded by foul-mouthed line cooks, late-night vices, and non-stop pressure, a reckless teenager stumbles into the raw grit and rock-and-roll pulse that defined his entire legacy. In English with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Coarse Language and Drug Use. The film contains an utterance of religious profanity that exceeds IMDA guidelines. The line has been muted by the distributor to be kept in line with guidelines.

filmhouse.title: Mysterious Skin (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: A teenage hustler and a young man obsessed with alien abductions cross paths, together discovering a horrible, liberating truth. Join us on 11 September in the Foyer for a Listening Party! Come by and soak in the lush music of MYSTERIOUS SKIN. We’re featuring the film’s evocative soundtrack, a deep cut collaboration between Robin Guthrie (Cocteau Twins) and Harold Budd, as well as tracks from shoegazers, Slowdive and Sigur Ros. Plus every one who comes receives a free complimentary MYSTERIOUS SKIN OST CD Keychain, which links out via NFC to the music, so you can take it home with you. Free RSVP Here! In English with English subtitles. Rated R21 for Mature Theme. TW: Contains themes of Sexual Violence.

filmhouse.title: Hereditary
filmhouse.description: Following the death of her secretive mother, miniature artist Annie Graham attempts to navigate her family's complex grief while maintaining a semblance of order in her secluded home. As disturbing, unexplainable events begin to target her children, the family plunges into a nightmare of escalating trauma, revealing sinister secrets about their ancestry. Directed by Ari Aster in his astonishing feature debut, this modern horror masterpiece captivated audiences and critics alike, earning Toni Collette widespread acclaim for her staggering central performance. Blending agonizing familial drama with relentless, visceral dread, the film crafts a haunting exploration of inherited trauma and inescapable fate. In English with Mandarin subtitles. Rated M18 for Some Nudity. TW: Contains depictions of self harm, animal cruelty and graphic scenes.

filmhouse.title: Love Letter (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: Still grieving the tragic loss of her fiancé Itsuki Fujii in a mountain climbing accident, Hiroko Watanabe sends a letter to his old childhood address in snow-covered Otaru, a home she believes no longer exists, hoping to send a message into the ether. To her shock, she receives a reply signed by "Itsuki Fujii." The respondent is not her late lover's ghost, but a female former classmate who shared his exact name. As the two women begin exchanging letters across the snowbound landscape, a tender, long buried portrait of forgotten youth, unrequited first love, and shared memory slowly unfurls. A foundational landmark of 1990s Asian cinema, Shunji Iwai’s feature debut became a massive cultural phenomenon across East and Southeast Asia, immortalized by Miho Nakayama’s double performance. Shot with a dreamlike, soft focus palette by the late cinematographer Noboru Shinoda, this new 4K digital restoration preserves every delicate detail. 4K remastering under the supervision of Fuji Television Network, Inc., with all analog and digital processes by Imagica Entertainment Media Services, Inc. Image digitization through high-resolution 4K scanning from the original 35mm camera negative. Restoration, color correction, and final sound finishing supervised by director Shunji Iwai. In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated PG Presented at Filmhouse as part of Japanese Film Festival, in partnership with the Singapore Film Society, Japan Creative Center and Japan Foundation

filmhouse.title: Wildwood
filmhouse.description: When her baby brother Mac is whisked away into an impenetrable, uncharted forest by a murder of crows, young Prue and her classmate Curtis ventures on a rescue mission. They stumble into a hidden realm where talking animals, mystical creatures, and warring factions vie for control. Drawn into an impending war orchestrated by the vengeful Countess Alexandra, Prue and Curtis must navigate treacherous alliances to save Mac and preserve the fragile balance of the magical wood. Directed by Travis Knight and produced by Laika(Coraline, Kubo and the Two Strings), this epic stop-motion fantasy adapts Colin Meloy’s beloved novel into the animation studio’s most ambitious feature to date. Featuring the voices of Carey Mulligan, Mahershala Ali, and Angela Bassett, the film blends tactile, hand-crafted puppet craft with sprawling scale, offering a thrilling and breathtaking coming-of-age adventure. In English Rated PG13 for Some Violence.

filmhouse.title: Look Back
filmhouse.description: In a quiet town, Fujino is a confident elementary school student whose clever four-panel manga strips earn her idolization from her peers. Her artistic ego is shaken when the school paper begins publishing the astonishingly detailed artwork of Kyomoto, a reclusive classmate who refuses to leave her room. What begins as bitter jealousy transforms into a life-changing friendship when the two young creators join forces, forging an intense creative bond that carries them through the triumphs, heartbreaks, and haunting tragedies of growing into adulthood. Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda (Shoplifters, Monster) and adapted from Tatsuki Fujimoto’s (Chainsaw Man) one-shot manga of the same name, this acclaimed live-action drama premiered at the Venice International Film Festival. Shot on tactile 35mm film, Kore-eda’s sensitive adaptation pairs nuanced performances with a deeply moving exploration of artistic creation, grief, and the quiet human connections that forever shape our lives. In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated PG for Brief Nudity.

upcoming.title: Henry's First Dates [THAI]
upcoming.description:
They say the first date is the most exciting moment in any relationship —
a feeling you only get once! Except for ‘Lucy’ (Minnie Nicha Yontararak), who’s
living her first date on repeat with ‘Henry’ (Nadech Kugimiya), a good-natured,
animal-loving guy with a bizarre condition: every time he wakes up, he can’t
remember anything from the day before. So, Lucy has to find a way to keep
wooing Henry, to make him fall in love with her every singe day. And that’s before
she even gets past his family and the people closest to him: Dad (Kiat Kitjaroen),
Ka-noon (Ble Patoomrach), and Auntie Su (Tipagorn Chaiprasit). Can Lucy make
Henry fall for her, again and again? Or will he forget her… forever?

upcoming.title: Sense And Sensibility
upcoming.description: From Focus Features and Working Title comes an irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles.

upcoming.title: The Mongoose
upcoming.description: A highly decorated combat vet, Ryan ''Fang'' Flanagan, is fleeing a murder scene at 130 miles an hour in a Mustang Shelby Super Snake GT350.

upcoming.title: The Weight
upcoming.description: Desperate to save what is left of his family, during the height of the Great Depression a battle-scarred veteran is hired to help smuggle a fortune in gold across 100 miles of impenetrable wilderness.

upcoming.title: V [CANTO]
upcoming.description: In the early 1990s, this city of desire, once "paved with gold", had fallen into a state of broken order and rampant crime. Worker Man Zi-Keung (Zhu Yilong) is determined to rewrite his fate.

upcoming.title: V [M]

upcoming.title: GODZILLA MINUS ZERO - IMAX Premiere Screening (JPN)
upcoming.description: One night. One day before everyone else. On the biggest screen. Join us for an exclusive IMAX Premiere Screening of Godzilla Minus Zero at Shaw Theatres Lido IMAX, a full day before it opens in cinemas. Feel every stomp and every roar in IMAX scale and take home premiere-night collectibles to mark the occasion!

upcoming.title: Godzilla Minus Zero [JPN]
upcoming.description:
War reduced Japan to zero, and Godzilla plunged it into minus. Two years have passed since then, and the country has faced agonizing struggles to achieve recovery and finally reclaim its daily life.

Just as humanity managed to cling to a hard-won peace, a new threat strikes, crushing hope in an instant.

There is no third time. Everything ends here.

upcoming.title: Paradise Lost [KOR]
upcoming.description:
My son, who disappeared nine years ago, has returned. But this is not the boy that I knew.
A bus carrying a group of children to camp vanishes. Only a few bodies are recovered before the case is cold-sealed. Among the grieving, So-young finds solace in reconnecting with her lost son, Sun-woo, through AR glasses. In the 9th year since his disappearance, the impossible happens: the real Sun-woo returns as an adult. But this shatters So-young’s world once more—the real son is a cold stranger; the virtual son needs her more than ever. At the crossroads of loving guilt and manic salvation, she faces a devastating choice.

upcoming.title: Ramayana: Rise of a Legend  [HINDI]
upcoming.description: Based on the celebrated ancient epic known to billions, Namit Malhotra's Ramayana tells the story of Rama, a prince bound by sacrifice; Ravana, an immortal king driven by vengeance; and the prophecy that binds their fates together. It stars Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi.

upcoming.title: Ramayana: Rise of a Legend [TAM]

In the film, The Cat takes on his toughest assignment yet… to cheer a pair of siblings struggling with their move to a new town.

upcoming.title: The Land Of Sometimes
upcoming.description: Twins Alfie and Elise find a magical Wish Watch on Christmas Eve and are swept by the Wish Collector into the musical Land of Sometimes, where they learn that wishes have consequences.

upcoming.description: This November, Johnny Depp is Ebenezer Scrooge. The name you know, the story you don’t. EBENEZER follows a miserly businessman who is forced through visions of the past, present, and future during a supernatural journey toward a chance at redemption.

upcoming.description: Nicholas Hoult and Pete Davidson are part of a group of bank robbers who share their heists on social media in this tongue-in-cheek thriller from the director of Bullet Train.

Her parents are separated and she lives with lazy, charming Pa (James Seah), naughty sister Ah Tian (Sydney Wong) and grumpy Ah Ma (Doreen Toh), while craving affection from aloof Mummy (Carrie Wong). Despite the chaos and conflict of her broken family, Ah Girl finds time to collect spiders, have a crush, and sell bubblegum, but can she stay true to herself when the adults threaten to make things worse?

upcoming.title: I Play Rocky
upcoming.description: Sylvester Stallone, then a failing actor, writes the ultimate underdog story and must fight for his chance to play the role of a lifetime - Rocky Balboa.

upcoming.title: George Michael - The Faith Tour
upcoming.description: George Michael was one of the most influential stars of his generation; his voice and songwriting defined an era. Assembled from rediscovered, previously unseen and unheard 35mm footage of his 1988 performance at the Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy, this new concert film captures George at the height of his creative power during the record-breaking Faith Tour. Expertly restored and remastered, the film transforms a defining cultural moment into a spectacular cinema experience. An original short film by Mary McCartney opens the feature, using newly discovered audio and imagery from 1986–1988 – the Faith era – creating a rare and intimate ‘time capsule’, offering a vivid insight into George’s mindset at this pivotal moment in his life.

upcoming.title: Disney's Hexed
upcoming.description: In Walt Disney Animation Studios' all-new magical coming-of-age saga, “Hexed,” an impulsive and unconventional teenage girl named Billie (voice of Hailee Steinfeld) discovers secret magical abilities which, once unleashed, hurtle her into a spectacle-filled journey out of suburbia and into a vast witch realm called Hexe. Forced to team up with her cautious mother, Alice (voice of Rashida Jones), they uncover family mysteries that could change the world of witches forever.

upcoming.title: Focker In-Law
upcoming.description: The circle of trust just got bigger. This November, comedy icon and Emmy winner Ben Stiller and two-time Oscar winner Robert De Niro reunite, joined by Grammy winner and Oscar nominee Ariana Grande, in Focker-In-Law, a new chapter in the blockbuster Meet the Parents franchise.

upcoming.description: A British professor witnesses a student's murder by secret police in 1981 Warsaw under martial law. She becomes a target while running through the city's streets, eventually forced to stop and take a stand.

upcoming.title: Bitter Christmas (SPANISH)
upcoming.description: In 2004, an ad director faces a turbulent Christmas weekend. In 2026, a filmmaker turns her story into a screenplay, blurring the lines between reality, fiction, and the people closest to him.

upcoming.title: Violent Night 2
upcoming.description: When Santa forgets the true meaning of Christmas, he finds himself in the heart of a lively mall community in desperate need of his help. Sapped of his magic, he'll need another way to take on the goons threatening the mall, and time is running out. Santa has to rediscover his faith in goodness and call in some last-minute reinforcements from the one person no baddie wants to tangle with: Mrs. Claus (Emmy and Golden Globe nominee Kristen Bell).

upcoming.title: Breakfast at Tiffany's (1961) (4K)
upcoming.description: Lovingly restored in stunning 4K. Elegant and eccentric, Holly Golightly lives off the gifts of gentlemen bewitched by her playgirl charm and searches Manhattan's socialite circles for a millionaire to marry. After meeting her new neighbour, Paul Varjak - a struggling writer and "kept" man financed by a steely older woman - the pair strike up a friendship which soon develops and threatens the delicate balance of both of their compromised lives.

upcoming.description: Dune: Part Three is based on the novel Dune Messiah by Frank Herbert and delivers the epic conclusion to Villeneuve’s trilogy.

upcoming.title: The Angry Birds Movie 3

upcoming.description: In Disney and Pixar's “Gatto,” the scrappy black cat Nero begins to question whether he’s lived the right lives after years of maneuvering the canal-ridden, superstitious city of Venice, Italy.
